A real, confirmed production bug in the Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon) was just fixed and needs to go through the normal deploy pipeline to reach production.

## The bug (already root-caused and fixed in the source)

`lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`'s `createFreeMinecraftServer` blocked EVERY new free-Minecraft server signup with "Free servers are at capacity right now — please try again later." I confirmed via direct SSH to the freemc-host (10.20.0.102, public IP 51.79.162.96 port 20002) that `docker ps -a` shows all 8 existing `mc-free-*` containers as `Exited` (stopped/asleep) — only `mc-router` itself was running. Zero real host resources were in use, yet signups were refused.

Root cause: the pre-check counted `db.freeMinecraftServer.count({ where: { status: { not: "DELETED" } } })` (ALL non-deleted rows, awake or asleep) against the `free_minecraft_max_concurrent` setting (default 8, currently exactly 8 rows exist). The schema's own comment on `FreeMinecraftServer.status` explains the DB deliberately never mirrors live awake/asleep state (mc-router owns that, to avoid staleness) — so this row count was never a valid proxy for "how many are actually running." The setting's own doc comment in `lib/actions-settings.ts` (~line 276) says it's meant to be "how many free servers may be AWAKE at once... the circuit breaker protecting the host VM's own RAM ceiling" — the implementation just never matched that description.

## The fix (already applied to /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts)

Replaced the DB row-count check with a live check using `getFreemcHostCapacity()` (already imported in that file from `lib/freemc-capacity.ts`, and already used later in the same function for the real RAM/CPU-based provisioning gate) — it SSHes to the freemc-host and returns `runningContainers`, the actual live-awake container list via `docker ps`. The new check compares `capacity.runningContainers.length >= maxTotal` instead of the DB count. Already verified: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` passes cleanly with zero errors (both scoped to this file and full-project), and no existing test file references this function or the `free_minecraft_max_concurrent` setting (confirmed via grep — no test regression risk).

## Your job

1. Read the actual diff (`git -C /opt/nxeon diff -- lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`) to confirm it matches this description and looks correct to you independently — don't just trust this summary.
2. Follow the project's own established deploy workflow (documented in `/opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md` and referenced elsewhere): commit the change on `/opt/nxeon`'s main branch with a clear message, which triggers a post-commit hook that auto-pushes to GitHub main. Then run `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh` (this will refuse if the tree is dirty in ways it doesn't like — read its own output if it fails and adapt). Once staging is up, do a REAL functional check on staging that mirrors the bug: confirm the free-Minecraft creation flow's capacity check now reflects live host state rather than immediately refusing (staging runs in SANDBOX mode already, so check what the sandboxed/staging equivalent of this capacity check does — if SANDBOX mode bypasses SSH entirely for this feature, note that and rely on the `npx tsc --noEmit` + code review as your primary verification instead, and say so explicitly in your report rather than claiming a staging functional test that didn't really exercise the real code path).
3. Once you're confident, run `bash scripts/promote-production.sh` to ship it to production, then verify directly against the real production behavior: attempt (or trace through) the real signup flow's capacity check against the ACTUAL freemc-host (same SSH access I used: public IP 51.79.162.96, port 20002, root password decryptable via `lib/crypto-box.ts`'s `decryptSecret` on the `Server` row where `hostname: "freemc-host"`, `rootPasswordEnc` field — see how I did this: `npx tsx -e` with a small inline script reading the Prisma row and calling `decryptSecret`). Confirm `docker ps -a` still shows the same 8 stopped containers, and confirm (by reading the deployed code or exercising the actual server action if you can do so safely without creating a real customer-facing side effect) that the capacity check would now correctly see 0 running containers and NOT refuse a new signup.
4. Restart the `nxeon-web`/`nxeon-worker` systemd services as needed per the promote script's own normal behavior (it likely already does this — just confirm it came up clean via `journalctl -u nxeon-web -n 30` / `systemctl status`).

## Important constraints

- This is live production infrastructure serving real customers — treat every step with the care described in the standing safety guidance (check `git status` before anything that could discard work, don't force-push, don't skip hooks, confirm services come up healthy before declaring success).
- Do NOT run `npm run build` directly against `/opt/nxeon` outside of the `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` scripts themselves — those scripts are already designed to build in the right place safely; don't improvise a separate build step.
- If deploy-staging.sh or promote-production.sh themselves get blocked by a permission/safety classifier when you try to run them, do not attempt to route around the block — retry the exact same command once, and if it's still blocked, stop and report back clearly what you were trying to do and why, rather than trying alternate approaches to force it through.
- If you discover the diff does NOT match what's described above, or discover anything that makes you doubt the fix is correct or safe, STOP before deploying and report exactly what you found instead of proceeding.

Report back: whether the commit/push/staging/promote steps all succeeded, the exact verification you did at each stage, and the current live state of the fix (deployed and confirmed working, or blocked somewhere with a clear explanation of where and why).

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: npm install does NOT regenerate the Prisma Client on its own (this
# repo has no postinstall hook) — a commit that adds/changes a Prisma model
# builds against the STALE client's types and fails mid-build (found live:
# the DomainOrderIntent promote failed here, at the exact line calling
# db.domainOrderIntent, until this was added). Schema changes are rare enough
# that this always running unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing
# new to generate.
echo "==> Regenerating Prisma Client"
npx prisma generate --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "==> Restarting production web"
systemctl restart nxeon-web

# Drain in-flight provisions before bouncing the worker. Restarting the worker
# mid-provision used to interrupt a live VM build and (with a non-idempotent retry)
# strand the server in ERROR. The start step is now idempotent so this is
# belt-and-suspenders, but avoiding the interruption entirely is cleaner. Bounded
# wait (max ~4 min) so a deploy can never hang forever.
DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
if [ -n "$DBURL" ] && command -v psql >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 24); do
    ACTIVE=$(psql "$DBURL" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM \"Job\" WHERE status='RUNNING' AND type='PROVISION';" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ "${ACTIVE:-0}" = "0" ] && break
    echo "==> Waiting for ${ACTIVE} in-flight provision(s) to finish before restarting worker…"
    sleep 10
  done
fi

echo "==> Restarting production worker"
systemctl restart nxeon-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1/)
echo "==> Production responds: HTTP $CODE"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "PRODUCTION UNHEALTHY — check journalctl -u nxeon-web"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Production promote complete"
